about.title: Computer Science & Finance · Boston College '29
about.photoAlt: Vincent Vo wearing a suit outdoors
about.bio: I'm a sophomore at Boston College studying Computer Science with a minor in Finance. I'm a Machine Learning Undergraduate Research Fellow at the PyTorch Connectomics Lab, a Boston College–Harvard collaboration led by Prof. Donglai Wei, where I help build the training data behind deep-learning models that segment mitochondria in electron microscopy images of the brain, and manage the teams that proofread it. Next summer I'm joining Fidelity Investments as a Leap Software Engineer Intern. I'm especially interested in where software meets finance, fintech and quantitative finance in particular. I graduated as valedictorian of Marianapolis Preparatory School in 2025.

highlights: Annotate and proofread mitochondria in large-scale electron microscopy volumes of the developing mouse cerebellum, producing labeled training data for deep-learning segmentation models
Project manager for the proofreading pipeline on the collaboration with Harvard's Lichtman Lab: onboard annotators, run quality control, track progress and deadlines
Lead the proofreading team for the H01 dataset
Develop features for the lab's annotation web app, including a mitochondria skeleton-length measurement tool
Presented my research to the Boston College Computer Science Department (Aug 2026)

projects.title: Maestrom
projects.shortDescription: A honeypot that detects AI hacking agents and keeps them occupied in a controlled tarpit.
projects.subtitle: Built at Hackachusetts 2026, the Mass AI Coalition's statewide AI hackathon.
detailDescription: Maestrom is a defensive honeypot built at Hackachusetts 2026, the Mass AI Coalition's statewide AI hackathon. It is designed to recognize AI-driven hacking agents and keep them occupied in a controlled tarpit rather than allowing them to reach real services.

I owned the gateway and detector—“the Brain”—for our four-person team. That layer evaluates incoming behavior, decides when traffic should be treated as an automated attack, and directs suspicious agents into the decoy environment.

projects.title: Butterfly Effect
projects.shortDescription: A two-layer GitHub visualization with a constellation “Sky” and a Spotify Wrapped-style “Ground.”
projects.subtitle: A team project built at FidHacks 2026, Fidelity's hackathon.
detailDescription: Butterfly Effect reframes GitHub activity as a two-part visual story. The “Sky” turns repositories and contributions into a constellation-inspired visualization, while the “Ground” presents a personal summary in a familiar Spotify Wrapped-style format.
We built the project as a team at FidHacks 2026, Fidelity's hackathon, combining data visualization and narrative design to make a developer's work easier to explore and share.

projects.title: Quantify
projects.shortDescription: An open-source app that lets Spotify users see which songs they have listened to most over different time ranges.
projects.subtitle: A full-stack Spotify listening-statistics app built with React, Express, and Spotify OAuth 2.0.
detailDescription: Quantify is an open-source project that lets users see which songs, artists, and genres they play most across different time ranges. It displays a user's profile, top artists, albums, and tracks for the previous four weeks, six months, and year.

The goal is to provide a free, editable alternative to subscription-based Spotify statistics tools, allowing people to customize the experience or learn from the code. As an avid music listener curious about my own listening habits, I wanted to solve the problem of detailed statistics being locked behind paid subscriptions.

I built Quantify with my former teacher and mentor, Jadorian Paul. The project gave me early experience with APIs, Git, Node.js, GitHub, JavaScript, React, and CSS. It grew into a full-stack application using React, Express, and Spotify OAuth 2.0.

projects.title: EcoLocate
projects.shortDescription: A web app that teaches responsible e-waste recycling and locates the nearest e-waste recycling center.
projects.subtitle: An accessible, community-focused platform connecting people with local e-waste recycling programs.
detailDescription: EcoLocate is a fully developed web platform that educates users about sustainable e-waste management and helps them find nearby recycling programs. The tool emphasizes accessibility and community-driven solutions by connecting users with organizations in their area. Its approach draws on circular-economy principles and ethical-disposal frameworks, with a focus on community engagement, data accuracy, and accessibility.

I built the interface with React, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. The browser's Geolocation API supplies a user's coordinates so the app can calculate distances to recycling centers. The backend uses Node.js and Express to handle server-side logic and API requests, including integration with Google's Places API. Project credentials are kept in environment variables with dotenv.

EcoLocate combines education, technology, and community action while drawing on existing infrastructure such as EPA recycling guidance and circular-economy models. Future versions could use analytics to predict regional e-waste trends, partner with manufacturers to promote device refurbishment, or bring the experience to a mobile app. The project demonstrates how localized technology can support wider systemic change.
